compliance.settlement_party: Fair Share Housing Center (FSHC) (Third Round, 2017); S. Hekemian Group LLC (intervenor, 2017); Hornrock Properties MPR LLC (intervenor, 2017); 2 Paragon Drive LLC (intervenor, 2017)

notes: HEFSP filed June 18, 2025 (BER-L-000750-25). Plan adopted June 4, 2025 per filing metadata. FSHC-challenged: As of June 4, 2025 (draft date), no final court order on Fourth Round obligation. DCA prospective need = 348. Borough recalculated to 237 units; Program Member Mendez recommended 237 on April 30, 2025. Credible range 180-237 per document; borough uses 237 as placeholder. Present need = 30 confirmed. RDP = 3 confirmed (VLA). Worst-case Unmet Need = 234 (based on 237 prospective need). Third Round: Settlement with FSHC November 14, 2017; Judgment of Compliance and Repose October 3, 2018. Third Round obligation ~255 units; RDP = 181; Unmet Need = 361 (per court order). Third Round unmet need addressed through overlay zones and set-aside ordinance per 2017 Settlement. Fourth Round Fair Share Plan (Chapter X) starts at page 40 of the full HEFSP but the only OCR'd document available is Part 1 (32 pages, Housing Element only). The sites for Chapters X-XII are NOT in the available OCR. From the Housing Element text we can confirm: (1) Nouvelle LLC 6-unit 100% affordable project approved by Planning Board December 2024 [site not further specified in Part 1]; (2) 42 units at 1 Glenview Road; (3) 18 units projected at 7 E. Grand Avenue. Candidate sites (Mercedes-Benz/Hekemian, Glenview, Sony/Hornrock, 2 Paragon Drive, KPMG overlay) are from Third Round settlement and cannot be verified at block/lot level from available documents. The GB Reso of June 24, 2025 endorsing the HEFSP was filed separately. Site block/lot data BLOCKED — Fair Share Plan section not available in filed OCR.

sources.excerpt: Montvale remains a land-constrained town and thus conducted a Vacant Land Adjustment analysis using tax data and environmental data to determine an RDP of 3 for the Fourth Round. The RDP subtracted from the FRO results in a worst-case Unmet Need of 234.
